$comment: Language servers of this pack. `config` is the fragment `factory init` merges into the app repo's .factory/config.json (lsp.servers entries, see docs/code-intelligence.md for every field). `optional` holds further fragments to merge by hand. `install` says how to get each server's binary, per OS (`all` = every OS); `factory lsp setup` prints these lines for a server it cannot find. `verified` says whether this file was proven by running the server through the factory or written from the server's documentation.

verified.how: Not run: jdtls is not installed on this machine. Written from the eclipse.jdt.ls README (the `jdtls` Python wrapper and its -data argument). Check the command line with `factory lsp check` before relying on it.

leased.java: yes: one JVM per checkout (1 GB and more) that imports the whole Maven or Gradle build.

linux: mkdir -p ~/.local/share/jdtls && curl -L https://download.eclipse.org/jdtls/milestones/<version>/<file from that folder>.tar.gz | tar -xz -C ~/.local/share/jdtls   # pick one milestone and keep it for the team
windows: Download the same milestone archive, extract it, and put its bin folder (jdtls.bat) on PATH; python3 is required.

requires: a JDK 21 or newer to run the server (the project may target an older one)
python3 for the jdtls wrapper script
Maven or Gradle wrapper files in the repository
notes: -data must be a directory per checkout: ${stateDir} is the checkout's own <git-dir>/lsp, so worktrees never share an Eclipse workspace.

The first start imports the build and downloads dependencies. Optional prepare: "prepare": {"command": "./mvnw", "args": ["-q", "-DskipTests", "dependency:go-offline"], "label": "resolving Maven dependencies"} (or "./gradlew" with ["--quiet", "dependencies"]).
Kotlin is not covered; add kotlin-language-server as its own entry if the repository needs it.
